title: Gate compiled regex replacement on the effective string dtype
answers: Why does replace ignore a compiled regex on Arrow-backed strings?
How should regex replacement decide which dtypes can match?
Why must regex replacement preserve NumPy bytes and non-string column dtypes?
Why does a compiled regex do nothing on categorical Arrow strings?
body:
Symptom: Series.replace or DataFrame.replace silently leaves Arrow-backed strings unchanged when given a compiled regex, although the string spelling substitutes correctly.
Root cause: pandas/core/internals/blocks.py:Block._replace_regex used a literal object/string allowlist for compiled patterns, excluding Arrow string dtypes before replacement ran.
Fix pattern: In Block._replace_regex, obtain the effective dtype through _regex_target_dtype, then require is_string_dtype(target_dtype) and target_dtype.kind != "S". Resolving categorical inputs to their categories' dtype lets compiled patterns reach the same replacement path as string patterns.
Constraints: Applies to Arrow string and large_string, including categorical variants. NumPy bytes and non-string Arrow columns must remain dtype-preserving no-ops. Supported Arrow string columns follow the existing object-upcast path for incompatible regex replacements. Dictionary-encoded Arrow strings, string_view, and incompatible non-regex replacements remain separate defects.
applies: Compiled regex eligibility in Series/DataFrame replacement, including categorical and mixed-dtype inputs.
